thread:
nina: heads-up, acme POC hitting mixed 401/403 after onboarding. started right after they pasted a token into env.

chris: timeline? any error snippets?

nina: pasted from their slack: 

chris: ```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_temp_abc123\" -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" \\n  -H \"X-Redwood-Project: acme-stream\" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/stream

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json

{
  \"error\": \"insufficient_scope\",
  \"message\": \"required scope 'inference:stream' not present\",
  \"code\": 403
}
```

chris: and a REST call to /v1/generate returned: 

nina: ```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_token\",
  \"message\": \"token_org_mismatch: token bound to 'dev-personal' (org: dev-labs), request org 'acme-corp'\",
  \"code\": 401
}
```

devops-bot: metrics: acme-poc (us-east-1) - token_errors: 22, avg RPS: 8.1, 95p latency: 240ms (last 10m).

elliot: sounds like two separate issues that coincided: 1) They used a personal/dev token from another org (token_org_mismatch). 2) For streaming they used a token without the streaming scope.

nina: can we confirm token scopes/check metadata without exposing full token? customer says token metadata shows scopes: [\"inference:invoke\"] and owner_org: \"dev-labs\".

elliot: yep that's the root cause. Remediation options: 
- generate an org-scoped service token in Acme org with scopes: inference:invoke,inference:stream and bind to project acme-stream if they want project-level access.
- or add X-Redwood-Project header matching the token's project if they intentionally used a project token.

elliot: example CLI: 
```
# create org-scoped service token with stream scope
rdwctl tokens create --org acme-corp --project acme-stream --scopes inference:invoke,inference:stream --name \"acme-poc-service\"
```

chris: customer also asked \"will switching to org-managed tokens change pricing or quotas?\"

sales-lead: quick answer for acme: no pricing change just for token type. Quotas/pricing follow the billing account/org. If they move to a different billing org that could change their tier.

nina: security asked for a one-line statement on auditability we can send to their security team.

elliot: \"All tokens are auditable: issuance, creator, scope, binding (org/project), last-used timestamp, and revocation events are recorded in the console and via the tokens API. Short-lived SSO tokens and KMS-backed rotation available for stricter policies.\"

chris: repro steps I used locally: 
```
# simulate stream call with wrong scope
export RW_KEY=sk_temp_abc123
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY\" -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" -H \"X-Redwood-Project: acme-stream\" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/stream | jq
```

chris: swap to sk_org_acme_xyz (org token with stream scope) -> calls succeed.

nina: customer rotated to new org token and added required header. they confirm stream works and REST calls are authorized. :tada:

devops-bot: monitoring: token_errors cleared for acme-poc (last 10m).

elliot: action items: 
- chris: send step-by-step repro + rdwctl example to their eng.
- nina: send security blurb to customer security contact.
- sales-lead: confirm in CRM that POC auth issue resolved.

sales-lead: thanks team. I'll follow up on pricing for dedicated capacity separately.

nina: closing this auth swarm. bye.
